correctness.rationale: For probability rows of the edge-rate-one walk, any coupling bounds the edgewise output difference by D times the input Lipschitz seminorm, also for complex functions. For every positive time the common mass of each pair of rows is positive and can be matched on the diagonal at zero cost. On a fixed finite graph there are finitely many edges, the norm is continuous, its value at zero is 1, and it tends to zero (normalize f at one vertex, so Lip(f) <= 1 implies ||f||∞ <= D, and use matrix convergence to the stationary projection). These facts imply the claimed strict uniform-in-time bound. For the tree lower bounds, independent rate-b and rate-one clocks produce, respectively, the b downward rate-one transitions and the unique parent or root-bridge transition, suppressing nonexistent moves. With no rate-one ring and at least h downward rings, the endpoint is a leaf on the starting side, or in the starting branch for the designated child. The union bound gives precisely the displayed epsilon at t=b^(-1/2). For even D=2h the root reaches a positive leaf except with probability at most epsilon+1/b (branch symmetry); the designated child reaches a negative leaf except with probability epsilon. The test function ranges from -h to h, yielding D(1-2 epsilon-1/b). For odd D=2h+1, the two root-started walks hit their respective leaf-value extremes except with probability epsilon each, giving D(1-2 epsilon). Each test function changes by one across every edge, and the farthest leaves certify the stated diameters, including h=1. Taking b to infinity at fixed h proves sharpness. This is an analytic proof; the frozen checker was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: No claim is made for a degree-normalized generator or for a limit uniform in diameter. The numerical examples are supplementary, not a certificate of the general theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the best possible bound from a widely used geometric parameter when local degree is unrestricted: adjacent starts can drive their averaged values almost the full graph diameter apart, even on trees. The parity constructions, explicit finite-branching estimates and strict gap on every fixed graph distinguish a class-wide extremum from a numerical example or a routine diameter upper bound.
residual_risks: The lower estimates are sufficient for the sharp envelope and are not a claim of optimal deficit at finite branching, size or degree.
